$doc: Content for <RoadmapList>. Six items, one horizon, each a number, a title and a gloss. Every string a reader sees lives here; the component holds no copy. THIS REPLACED A THREE-COLUMN TABLE on 1 Sep and the reason was countable rather than aesthetic: the table had fourteen cells and ELEVEN OF THEM RESTATED EARLIER SECTIONS. Its `built` column was the eight frames the reader had just walked through in section 05, and its `replaced` column was section 02's three friction beats - the deleted $replacedDoc said so in its own words, 'a callback, not new information'. Only the three milestone names were new, which is why the module read long.
$horizonDoc: THE DECK HAS TWO HORIZONS AND THE STUDY HAD ONLY EVER SHOWN ONE. Deck p23 lists three short-term priorities and four longer-term vision items. Every version of this module, through the table that shipped until 1 Sep, used the short-term column and dropped the rest. That mattered because THE VISION COLUMN IS WHAT EVIDENCES THE CLAIM THE SECTION NOW MAKES: Paul set a direction, and a direction is the vision, not the fix list. So section 06 stopped being an outcome beat and became the plan; section 05 keeps the evidence and section 07 keeps where it landed. THE COST OF THAT, STATED SO IT IS NOT RESTORED: the old caption's line 'Every feature here is on a 2019 screen' IS DEAD, because items 04 to 06 were never built. THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS SAYING THEY HAVE NO SCREENS, WHICH THIS ENTRY CLAIMED UNTIL 1 Sep AND WHICH THE PAGE DISPROVES. Item 06 is 'Enhancing Browse with filters for delivery options', and section 05's walk mounts browse--page, whose left rail carries the Delivery and Pickup filter, and browse--facet, which is that filter close up. SCREENS EXISTING AND THINGS BEING BUILT ARE DIFFERENT FACTS on this page: the walk's frames are Paul's white-label design work rather than shipped brand UI, which section 05 already establishes. Conflating the two produced both of the caption defects fixed on 1 Sep. A later pass that reads the first three items and reaches for that sentence would be making a claim about three items that were never built.
$orderDoc: ORDER IS THE DECK'S AND IT IS SETTLED, EXTENDED FROM THREE ITEMS TO SIX ON 1 Sep. Deck p23 lists inventory sync, then delivery date accuracy, then reduce split shipments in the short-term column, then the four longer-term items in the order carried here. Paul confirmed the first three on 25 Aug and supplied the six-item sequence on 31 Aug as his own de-duplication of the deck, WHICH LISTS 'Reduce split shipments' IN BOTH COLUMNS. Do not restore the duplicate and do not reorder. THE REASONING FOR THE ORDER WAS ASKED FOR AND DOES NOT EXIST. This entry used to say only that the reasoning 'is not' settled, which reads as a gap waiting to be filled. It is not a gap. Paul was asked directly on 31 Aug whether he knows why inventory sync precedes date accuracy, and HE DOES NOT. So the page prints the order, attributes it to the roadmap, and explains nothing, and THAT IS THE FINAL STATE. No caption, gloss or comment gains a why-this-order clause. A plausible engineering story could be written here and it would be an invention. RAISING THE ORDINAL TO 28px ON 1 Sep MAKES THE ORDER LOUDER AND DOES NOT CHANGE THIS. The settled ruling forbids drawing CAUSALITY, not order; printing 01 through 06 prominently states a sequence the deck states, and states nothing about why.
$nameDoc: ITEM 06 DROPS THE DECK'S TRAILING & "Shop My Store", AND THE NAME IS NOT LOST - the gloss says 'her store', which is the same capability in plain language rather than as an internal product name. THE RULE IS THAT A PROPER NOUN NEEDS A REFERENT ON THE PAGE. Every other item here is self-describing, so a reader parses it cold; an internal codename with no picture beside it reads as insider shorthand. IT ALSO DISSOLVES A PROVENANCE PROBLEM RATHER THAN DEFERRING IT. The deck lists Shop My Store as unbuilt longer-term vision, while store--ribbon.png is a 2019 capture whose own button reads Shop Your Store. Either it shipped after the deck or that screen is a design, and NOBODY KNOWS WHICH. With the name off the page there is no contradiction to resolve. THE PAIRING IS THE RULE: IF THE BAND COMES BACK, THE NAME COMES BACK WITH IT. No image, no name. Neither half is reversible on its own, and that is why this is recorded beside the content rather than in a commit message.
$captionDoc: THE GLOSS SCOPES THE LIST AND MUST NOT BE SOFTENED. Three of the six were never built, and a reader given no marker assumes all six shipped. IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REPEAT SECTION 07, which already says 'I left URBN that November. Most of what shipped, shipped without me, and I will not claim the execution.' 06 SCOPES THE LIST; 07 SCOPES THE STUDY. THE 'TWO SECTIONS APART' ARGUMENT THIS ENTRY USED TO CARRY IS DEAD AND MUST NOT BE USED TO RESTORE THE DATE. It was only ever half true - the departure was always stated twice and distance was the only thing carrying it - and removing the measurement section on 1 Sep deleted the distance. The caption said 'by the time I left that November' about 74px from section 07's 'I left URBN that November' at 390, roughly 130px at desktop. The date is section 07's; the caption dropped it on 1 Sep and now says 'when I left', which scopes the list without dating anything twice. 'IN BUILD' RATHER THAN 'ON SCREENS', FOR THE SAME PASS AND A DIFFERENT REASON. Paul ruled that the first three were in active build when he left and 04 to 06 existed as direction and design only. 'On screens' read as a build-state claim and failed against the page, because item 06's browse filters ARE on screens in section 05's walk. See $horizonDoc. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: that the teams kept building after Paul left. He has not said he knows that, so the study does not say it. EVERY GLOSS IS WRITTEN AS WHAT THE ITEM DOES, NEVER AS WHAT SHIPPED. That is what lets six items sit in one horizon without any of them claiming execution, and a gloss drifting into past tense during an edit would start making the claim section 07 explicitly refuses. Checked mechanically, not by eye.
$retainedDoc: store--ribbon.png IS RETAINED AND UNMOUNTED, ON PURPOSE. It was a <BentoBand> in section 06 until 1 Sep and nothing references it now. It is not deleted because the question that unmounted it is open rather than answered: the deck lists 'Shop My Store' as unbuilt longer-term vision while that band is a 2019 capture whose own button reads Shop Your Store, so either it shipped after the deck or the screen is a design, and nobody knows which. An unreferenced 137KB asset is cheap; a deleted one that turns out to be wanted is a re-cut from source. IF IT COMES BACK, ITEM 06 GETS ITS CODENAME BACK IN THE SAME PASS - see $nameDoc, which owns that pairing. ONE CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING RATHER THAN ACTING ON: the band carried scrollFloor={1700}, one of only two live scrollFloor instances across the four studies. Unmounting it leaves ONE, in uscg-bard/theme2-grid-manifest.json, which turns the mobile horizontal-scroll question from a cross-study sweep into a single instance. Paul has filed that; nothing here acts on it.
